text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthWhy Do Obese People With Alzheimer’s Live Longer?The “obesity paradox” strikes againJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 6, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThere’s a bit of a mystery surrounding obesity. Even though it’s a risk factor for a whole host of health problems, it also seems to offer some mortality benefits. For example, obese individuals diagnosed with kidney disease, pulmonary embolisms, cardiovascular disorders, and more have a reduced risk of dying. Now this so-called “obesity paradox” has popped up in a new study of Alzheimer’s patients, as well. Public health researchers made the discovery after examining health data dating from 1998 to 2022 from more than 4,500 Alzheimer’s-free people 51 and older enrolled in the Health and Retirement Study. They found that those who were obese at the time of their Alzheimer’s diagnosis were also less likely to die. Overweight individuals (with a BMI from 25 to 29.9) had a 16 percent lower risk, those with class 1 obesity (BMI of 30 to 34.9) had a 27 percent lower risk, and those with class 2 and 3 obesity (BMI equal to or greater than 35) had a 22 percent lower risk.Read more: “Why Do More Women Than Men Develop Alzheimer’s?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
